text: The ticket is hers, not mine. <break time="0.8s" /> So she would hold on to every penny. <break time="0.8s" /> And give me only a hundred roubles. <break time="0.8s" /> He thought bitterly. <break time="0.8s" /> For the first time in his life. <break time="0.8s" /> He noticed that his wife had grown old and plain. <break time="0.8s" /> While he still felt young and healthy. <break time="0.8s" /> He thought of her relatives. <break time="0.8s" /> Who would come crawling. <break time="0.8s" /> With false smiles. <break time="0.8s" /> Begging for money. <break time="0.8s" /> As soon as they heard the news. <break time="0.8s" /> It was his wifes face, too. <break time="0.8s" /> That now seemed hateful to him. <break time="0.8s" /> And he looked at her. <break time="0.8s" /> Not with a smile but with anger. <break time="0.8s" /> Masha looked back at him. <break time="0.8s" /> With the same anger. <break time="0.8s" /> For she had her own dreams. <break time="0.8s" /> And knew. <break time="0.8s" /> Who would try to grab her winnings first. <break time="0.8s" /> Her eyes seemed to say that it was easy to dream. <break time="0.8s" /> With other peoples money. <break time="0.8s" /> And that he had better not touch it. <break time="0.8s" /> To annoy her. <break time="0.8s" /> Ivan glanced. <break time="0.8s" /> At the fourth page. <break time="0.8s" /> And read out in triumph. <break time="0.8s" /> Series 9, 499, number 46, not 26. <break time="0.8s" /> At once hatred and hope both disappeared. <break time="0.8s" /> And their rooms seemed. <break time="0.8s" /> Dark, small, and low. <break time="0.8s" /> And the evenings long and dull. <break time="0.8s" /> There are crumbs and bits of paper everywhere. <break time="0.8s" /> And the rooms are never swept. <break time="0.8s" /> Grumbled Ivan. <break time="0.8s" /> So a man is forced to go out.
